chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will resurrect a group of people from their graves on the Day of Resurrection with their hands tied to their necks, unable to reach even the width of a fingernail with them. With them will be angels taunting them with severe taunt, saying: 'These are the ones who withheld a little good from a lot of good! These are the ones whom Allah gave, but they withheld the right of Allah in their wealth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of withholding Zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the spiritual consequences of stinginess, specifically linking the physical restraint of the hands to the failure to purify wealth through Zakat. The angels' taunt underscores the principle that withholding a small obligatory portion constitutes a denial of Allah's right, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence on the sanctity of wealth. This emphasizes that Zakat is not merely a tax but a means of spiritual liberation from the bondage of materialism.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High would be Resurrecting a group of people from their graves on the Day of Judgement, with their hands tied tight upon their necks, not being able to take anything with them from even a distance of a fingertip. With them would be Angels taunting them with severe taunts, saying: ‘These ones are those who prevented a little good from a lot of good! These are the ones whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> had Given, but they prevented a Right of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in their wealth’.
en.sarwar: 22. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ayyub ibn Nuh from ibn Sinan from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Allah, the most Holy, the most High, will raise a people from their graves, on the Day of Judgment, their hands tied up to their necks and they will not be able to take anything even from a distance of one finger. Angels along with them censure them severely and say, “These were the ones who withheld a small amount of good, which could gain for them a great deal of good. These are those who refused to pay the right of Allah from their wealth.’”
